costGuide.title: Renault H4M Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an H4M in an E-Tech hybrid application typically takes 7-9 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes, as high-voltage system isolation is required.

failures.title: Renault H4M Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear - 2016-Present
items.whatHappens: The H4M (and its Nissan HR16DE twin) uses a timing chain that is generally durable, but high-mileage units can experience chain stretch or tensioner wear. This typically presents as a brief rattling noise on cold starts. If left unaddressed, it can lead to erratic valve timing and a illuminated check engine light.
items.repairVsReplace: A standalone timing chain kit replacement typically costs £600-£1,200. However, if the chain has jumped teeth and caused piston-to-valve contact, a full H4M engine replacement is the only viable route.

items.title: Ignition Coil and Spark Plug Wear - 2016-Present
items.whatHappens: As a naturally aspirated petrol engine, the H4M is susceptible to standard ignition wear. Failing ignition coils or worn spark plugs manifest as misfires, rough idling, and a slight drop in fuel efficiency, which is particularly noticeable in the hybrid system's transition between electric and petrol power.
items.repairVsReplace: These are routine maintenance items. Replacing the ignition coils and spark plugs is highly cost-effective (£150-£300) and rarely justifies a full engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The H4M is fundamentally a very robust and simple naturally aspirated unit. Unlike the turbocharged 1.2 TCe (H5Ht) it indirectly replaced in the hybrid lineup, the H4M lacks complex turbochargers and high-pressure direct injection, making it significantly less prone to catastrophic carbon buildup or turbo failures .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the H4M
variants.intro: The H4M is a Specific engine code, but it is frequently confused with the older 1.6 16V (K4M) or the 1.2 TCe turbocharged engines (H5Ft/H5Ht). The H4M in the E-Tech hybrid is specifically adapted with unique crankshaft interfaces, a specific flywheel, and mounting points designed to mate with the electric motor and the dog-box transmission. Where to find the code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bell housing, and is also printed on the vehicle’s VIN plate under the bonnet. It is listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code".

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement H4M - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used H4M is a viable option for the engine block itself, but caution is required regarding the hybrid interface components. Ensure the replacement unit includes the correct E-Tech specific flywheel and starter-generator (HSG) mounting points. Explore our used engine options only with a pre-purchase compression test.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the H4M. A proper reconditioned unit will address the common high-mileage wear points, including a refreshed timing chain kit, new ignition coils, and verified hybrid interface components, restoring the engine to near-factory reliability. View our reconditioned engine services .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original H4M block has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure (bent valves) or if the hybrid integration points are damaged. It allows for the installation of upgraded components during the strip-down. Learn more from our rebuilt engine specialists .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing through our network ensures your H4M is matched correctly, comes with a minimum 12-month warranty, and can be installed by vetted specialists nationwide via our supply and fit network .
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The H4M is found in the Renault Clio V and Captur II E-Tech hybrids, which have typical UK values ranging from £10,000 to £22,000. Because a reconditioned replacement can cost upwards of £1,355 fitted, it represents a very small fraction (under 15%) of the vehicle's value. Replacement is highly financially viable and strongly recommended over scrapping for these modern hybrid hosts.

items.question: How much does a Renault H4M engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Renault H4M engine typically costs between £900 and £1,800 for supply only, or £1,355 to £2,385 fully fitted by an independent specialist . Used units start around £300-£700 but require careful inspection of the hybrid interface components. Full rebuilds addressing timing chain and ignition wear range from £1,500-£2,500. Labour typically takes 7-9 hours, with additional time required for high-voltage system isolation.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the H4M engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues with the H4M are timing chain stretch and standard ignition wear, typical of high-mileage naturally aspirated engines. A failing timing chain or tensioner usually presents as a brief rattling noise on cold starts. Ignition coil and spark plug wear can cause misfires, particularly noticeable during the hybrid system's power transitions. Neither issue is usually catastrophic if addressed early, but an ignored chain failure can bend valves and write off the engine.

items.question: Which Renault models use the H4M engine?
items.answer: The H4M is the core combustion engine for the Renault E-Tech full hybrid powertrain, fitted to several modern models from 2020 onwards. It is most commonly found in the Renault Clio V and Captur II E-Tech Hybrid variants. It is also used in the Renault Arkana E-Tech Hybrid. Always verify your V5C, as this specific hybrid-adapted H4M is not interchangeable with older non-hybrid 1.6L engines.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned H4M engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned H4M is strongly recommended over a used unit to ensure the hybrid interface components and timing chain are in optimal condition. A proper reconditioned unit will feature a refreshed timing chain kit, new ignition components, and verified E-Tech specific flywheel and mounting points. A used engine is only viable if it comes with documented proof of a recent timing chain replacement and hybrid system health check.

items.question: Is the Renault H4M the same as the Nissan HR16DE?
items.answer: Yes, the Renault H4M and Nissan HR16DE are the exact same physical engine, developed jointly by the Renault-Nissan alliance. The internal architecture, block, head, and replacement parts are identical across both brands. The only differences are the ECU mapping and minor ancillary bracket placements to suit specific Renault E-Tech or Nissan engine bays.
